text: Lesson 10 locked the storage account and bucket down to deny-by-default and blocked public access entirely. That means the VM from Lesson 9 has no way to reach either one right now — which isn't a bug to fix by opening things back up. It's the correct intermediate state: compute and storage both exist, locked down, waiting for one specific, scoped connection.

az vm identity assign gives the VM a system-assigned managed identity — the exact mechanism the identity chapter covered for Key Vault, now applied to storage, with no password or key generated or stored anywhere. That identity is managed entirely by Azure, created alongside the VM and removed automatically if the VM is deleted. role assignment create then grants that identity the Storage Blob Data Contributor role, scoped to this one storage account specifically, not the resource group or the subscription. The application authenticates as the VM at runtime and never handles a storage account key at all.

AWS uses the identical pattern the IAM fundamentals chapter already covered for exactly this use case — an EC2 instance reaching S3 with no embedded key. A role gets a trust policy that lets the EC2 service assume it, a permission policy scoped narrowly to the one bucket from Lesson 10, and both get wrapped in an instance profile attached to the running instance. AWS's STS issues temporary credentials behind the scenes automatically, so there's still no long-lived access key sitting in a config file anywhere on the instance.

This is the connection the last three lessons were building toward — a VM or EC2 instance in the right subnet, reaching storage locked down by default, through an identity-based grant scoped to exactly one resource. No embedded credential exists anywhere in that chain for anyone to leak, commit to source control, or forget to rotate.

That's the whole chapter's deployment order: network first, then compute into it, then storage locked down, then one scoped identity connecting the two. Next up: proving all of that actually works, with a real smoke test, before calling this environment done.
